messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: ggplot2 help for plotting trajectories
parts:
Does anyone know how to plot a trajectory using ggplot2.
(I'm writing up the manual for the ODE solver.)

I tried to use the commands and data given on page 10 of

http://had.co.nz/stat480/lectures/14-graphics-qplot.pdf

but they didn't work. There are no lines connecting things for
any of the options. I hate these descriptions in R because
they never mention the libraries needed (in this case, reshape
for the melt() function).

Daniel showed me how to do it in base graphics, but I think
the output's incredibly ugly compared to ggplot2 and the other
plots in the manual are in ggplot2, so it'd be nice to be consistent.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ggplot2 help for plotting trajectories
parts:
Never mind. ggplot2 broke backward compatibility at
some point, so that the suggestion in the pdf doc:

qplot(a, b, data = df, type = "path")

is now broken, and the required incantation is now

qplot(a, b, data = df, geom=c("point","path"))

- Bob
